hints: Look at where each sequence starts. Where is the natural pacemaker of the heart located, and so what must come first?
Remember the functional order: atria must contract first, then there is a short delay at the AVN before the impulse is carried rapidly down to the base of the ventricles by Purkyne tissue.
walkthrough:
**Start at the pacemaker**

Think of the sinoatrial node (SAN) as the spark plug. It is in the wall of the right atrium and it initiates each wave of excitation. So any correct sequence must start with the sinoatrial node.

**Spread across the atria, then pause at the AVN**

The wave spreads across the muscle of the right and left atria, so they contract together and push blood into the ventricles. The impulse is then picked up by the atrioventricular node (AVN), which imposes a short delay to let the ventricles fill.

**Shoot down to the ventricles**

From the AVN the impulse travels rapidly down the bundle of His and out through the Purkyne tissue in the ventricular walls. This makes the ventricles contract from the base upwards. That gives: sinoatrial node to atria to atrioventricular node to Purkyne tissue.

options.A: This starts with the atria before the SAN, which is backwards. The SAN generates the impulse that causes the atria to contract.
options.B: This is the correct order. SAN initiates, atria contract, AVN collects the impulse after a delay, then Purkyne tissue carries it to the ventricles.
options.C: Purkyne tissue cannot come before the AVN. The impulse must pass through the AVN first before it can reach the Purkyne tissue.
options.D: This misses out the AVN and its vital delay. The impulse must go via the AVN before reaching Purkyne tissue to allow time for ventricular filling.
